stemMd: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 180 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?
explanationMd: Using work done by the gas as positive, the first law is ΔU = Q − W. Thus ΔU = 500 − 180 = +320 J. The positive result means the gas retains some of the absorbed energy internally.

distractorRationale.b: This adds work done by the gas instead of subtracting it.
distractorRationale.d: The absorbed heat exceeds the energy transferred out as work.
distractorRationale.e: This gives both energy transfers the wrong signs.
distractorRationale.c: This reports the work alone and ignores heat.
